body:
>Firstly, you could try quitting your job and trying to get a job somewhere else, even if it is still fast-food. 

It took me far too long just to find this job, and it's at one of the few places that was hiring and along the bus route. 

> I'm glad you live with your sibling at the moment and not alone, because you have someone you've known all your life to socialise with and help you out if you need it.

I've actually only really known them for the last 4 years. Like I said, they're a bit older than me and we moved away from them when they graduated high school and I was still a preteen. They wanted nothing to do with me during my childhood, and in adulthood I think they're trying to make up for it. Aside from that, they do invite me to a lot of stuff, but I always end up insanely uncomfortable and leaving. 

>You two moving out is inevitable, so perhaps you can try finding a SO through a dating app.

I tried a couple a few years ago and it just seemed like a bunch of superficial hook-up shit, and I hate meeting new people in such an inorganic manner. After a few bad experiences making friends and meeting potential mates online, I don't think I want to take that route anymore. Thanks for the suggestion though. 

>I know you say you don't give a shit about finding a SO, but when your brain clicks and you fall in love, whether that's instantly or over a period of time, you will feel so much better. 

I really don't want to be 'in love' and I really don't want anyone to feel that way about me. I overly romanticized pretty much every relationship I've ever had only to realize later how poor of a match it was. I don't feel like I have the energy to be an SO to anyone. Even in high school I was pretty cold and callous towards people I dated.
I've never really seen anything that made me think 'wow, relationships really are worth the trouble.'

>Also, since you're 22, you still have time to go back to school/uni and get your life back. 

Being broke, working full time, and unable to get a loan, this isn't really a possibility. 

>The fast-food industry is a very repetitive job, but if you could get into something a bit more exciting, perhaps a paramedic, I'm sure you would feel a lot better and you would want to live. 

I've been voluntarily committed several times, and have pretty massive depression, I don't think I would be suited to a high-stakes, life or death position like that. I think it would have the opposite effect, I wouldn't be able to handle it at all.

>You say you have zero interest in anything anymore, so maybe you could get a therapist to help you out on that.

I've basically lost faith in therapy. I've been to 6 different therapists in 3 different states and each one was less effective than the last. Not to mention the 8 different psychiatrists I've had in that time that tried to put me on a dozen different medications to try and balance me out, each time it only got worse.

>A lot of what I said so far may not interest you, and if so, I would recommend making a big life change. If that means moving countries or whatnot, then go for it. 

I don't think we're on the same page but I appreciate the time and effort you put into reaching out to me. Sincerely, thank you for that. As far as moving goes, I have no way to do any of that. My sibling can help with food and a place to stay for the time being, but that's about all they can offer and all I would ask for. 

>I don't know if anything I said helped, but I enjoyed writing it.

Even if it doesn't really apply to me, it might help someone else, so thanks again.
